newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels take east Zaire town, conflict spreads.
newsitem.headline: Rebels take east Zaire town, conflict spreads.

text.p: Tutsi rebels have seized the town of Uvira in eastern Zaire after two days of battles with Zairean troops, military sources and Burundi state radio said on Saturday.
The battle for Uvira was one piece of the complex multi-sided conflict in eastern Zaire which on Saturday appeared to be spreading through the 1.1 million Rwandan refugees based in the area.
For the first time, large numbers of Rwandan refugees were reported to be on the move in the Goma region north of here.
"Some 200,000 refugees from Kibumba camp near Goma are heading down the road towards the city," said a U.N. official, who declined to be identified.
He quoted reports from aid workers as describing the town of Rutshuru north of Goma city as "a war zone" and said it appeared the attackers were former Tutsi residents of the Masisi region near Goma.

It was the first large refugee movement from Rwandan camps around Goma, the capital of North Kivu province, since fighting erupted in eastern Zaire more than a week ago between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops.
Nearly 300,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees were uprooted from their camps in South Kivu province by the fighting.

In Bukavu, 100 km (60 miles) to the north of Uvira, four mortar blasts were heard on Saturday morning and the United Nations ordered an evacuation of aid workers from the city because of increasing insecurity, a U.N. spokeswoman said.

"There are orders from the U.N. security office in New York to carry out a total or partial evacuation of staff from Bukavu to Entebbe airport in Uganda today," said Brenda Barton, a spokeswoman for the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) in Nairobi.
A plan to airlift food to Bukavu from Uganda later on Saturday for refugees displaced by the fighting was put on hold, she said.
Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels have been fighting Zairean troops in eastern Zaire for more than a week. They say they are resisting pressure from the Zairean authorities to expel them from the country.
The Banyamulenge arrived in the region up to 200 years ago but ethnic tensions have become acute in the aftermath of the 1994 genocide and civil war in neighbouring Rwanda.
About 1.1 million Hutus fled to Zaire from Rwanda in fear of reprisals for the killing by Hutus of up to an estimated one million Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko has been absent from the country for more than two months, receiving cancer treatment in Switzerland, and his long illness is fuelling the crisis.
Zairean troops have been pulling back towards Bukavu, capital of South Kivu province, in recent days as the rebels advance from the south.
Saturday was the first time mortar explosions were clearly heard in Bukavu since fighting in eastern Zaire broke out.
The blasts came from the area near Panzi camp, 10 km (six miles) south of the city centre, but it was unclear whether the fire was incoming or outgoing.
Panzi camp houses 2,000 Hutu former soldiers of the Rwandan army and 5,000 family members who fled into Zaire in 1994.

Militiamen blocked the roads in the south of the city and civilians started stoning journalists. More than 100 militiamen, youths armed only with pieces of wood, had been rounded up to defend the city.

Uvira, a port at the northern end of Lake Tanganyika near the border with Burundi, is the biggest town reported to be in rebel hands, though its present population is unknown. Journalists have been barred from the area.
